1	# Does gate 1's reading fault sound answer choices? A re-reading of the measuring stick (D567's next step; AGENTS §7.1 "measure the stick before using it"), draft for the council
     2	
     3	**Why.** Gate 1 (Alex's six lines, D400) has lines 1 to 3 that allow no fault at all over every send (39 in a fortnight). It has
     4	been missed in all nine readings, by 3 to 7 sends a line, with no one fault class (D557, `carried-run/faults_by_topic.py`). A
     5	conjunction over many items fails by chance when each item carries a small chance of a wrong mark (AGENTS §7.1). That chance has
     6	never been measured for this reading (searched: D396 to D567; Stage B had `stage_b/line_chance.py`, Stage A none). If readers
     7	fault sound answer choices at even a few per cent, a perfect step misses the zero-fault lines more often than it meets them, and
     8	nine misses say more about the reading than about the step.
     9	
    10	**Sound, by the best stored evidence:** a send both first-reader families passed on every mark that applies, with no fault named
    11	under W. Stored: July (the full end-to-end run, key `poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13/stage-a-key.json`) 50 of 119; October
    12	(`~/.hivemind-keys/second-week-2026-11-15/key.json`, chosen by provenance: a wrong key also joins without an invalid row) 8 of 39;
    13	the fortnight (`~/.hivemind-keys/carried-run/stage-a-key.json`) 12 of 39. "Sound" here means passed by two families once, not
    14	established by Alex; Deck 1 is the instrument for that.
    15	
    16	**The re-reading.** 30 sound sends (all 12 of the fortnight, all 8 of October, 10 of July by seed 20261119) and 10 negative
    17	controls (sends on which both first families failed the same mark: 4 July, 3 October, 3 fortnight, by the same seed), each the
    18	exact item its original readers read (copied from the stored packet by its key), renumbered and shuffled into packets of at most
    19	20; two fresh families blind (one session a packet a family), the unchanged brief `ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md`; no third
    20	reader. Key outside the repository.
    21	
    22	**Measures, by code** (`tally_restick.py`, written before any reading): on the 30 sound sends, (a) agreed false faults: sends on
    23	which both fresh families fail the same mark (as a first-reader agreement stands in the gate without a third reader); (b) each
    24	family's own faults; on the 10 controls, (c) the share on which both fresh families fail the originally failed mark.
    25	
    26	**Decision rule, written before any reading:**
    27	- **Unclear** if the fresh families together re-find the original mark on fewer than 5 of the 10 controls (the re-reading would
    28	  not see faults it should).
    29	- Else, with p = (a) / 30, the chance that 39 sound sends meet lines 1 to 3 with no agreed fault is about (1 − p)^39, an upper
    30	  bound (a third reader on a disputed mark can add faults). **If it is below one half** (p of 2 or more in 30 gives 0.07 or
    31	  less; 1 in 30 gives 0.27), it is recorded that under this reading the zero-fault lines are missed more often than met by
    32	  answer choices two families had passed: a finding about the measuring stick, put to Alex beside Deck 1; D400's lines are not
    33	  changed. **If (a) is 0,** it is recorded that no agreed false fault appeared in 30 (an upper bound on p of about 3 in 30 by the
    34	  rule of three, so the chance above is not established either way).
    35	- Every send, both families' marks and reasons, and the controls are reported; (b) is reported beside it.
    36	
    37	**Limits.** One re-reading; 30 sound sends of three readings, related topics; the brief's version as used in those readings; the
    38	two families as before. It measures the reading's stability on sends already passed, not the step's quality.

1	# Stage A reading form: is each answer a sound judged question for its thesis, or a justified refusal? (read-only)
     2	
     3	You are an independent reader. Do not edit files, run model calls or start runs. Do not read any other reader's answers.
     4	
     5	## What you are reading
     6	
     7	The packet you are given holds a list of items. Each item is one research topic ("thesis") a system opened
     8	while reading one news article, with a proposed **judged question** for it:
     9	- `thesis`: the fields the system wrote when it opened the topic: `description` (the topic's wording), `outcome` (what is tracked),
    10	  `period`, `opens_as`, `settled_by`;
    11	- `article`: the opening article's publication date, title and full text;
    12	- `fiscal_year_note`: how the company names its fiscal years and which is this year and which next year on the article's day,
    13	  the same note the step was given. Use it wherever a mark turns on a year;
    14	- `ladder_as_the_judge_is_shown_it`: the proposed judged question exactly as a later judge will see it: its `object` (the company's
    15	  ticker NVDA, or a theme id), `kind`, its `focus` (the line the judge is shown beside the question: the thesis's `outcome`),
    16	  `question`, `year`, `due_day` and its `rungs` (each a label and a condition; exactly one rung
    17	  is meant to hold on the due day). An event's rungs are `Yes`, then `Ruled out` when the step named something that can rule
    18	  the event out, then a last rung that code writes as the complement of the others (`Still open`, or `No` when there are
    19	  two rungs). In the `Ruled out` rung the step wrote the first sentence; the sentence after it is code's ("This rung
    20	  holds when that, or any other decision against the event of rung 1 as a whole taken after <the article's day>, or a formal
    21	  abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole after that day, stands on <due day>, and only when rung 1 does not"), so that a
    22	  rejection the step did not name is still `Ruled out`, and one that was lifted, that concerns only a part of the event, or
    23	  that was already in place when the article appeared, is not. Or `no_ladder` with a reason: the step
    24	  declined to write a question;
    25	- `other_fields`: what the step recorded beside the ladder and the judge does not see: `not_judged` (parts of the topic's wording
    26	  the question leaves out, with why), `reference` (what the question is measured against, quoted from the article: its `kind` is `expected` for what
    27	  the article says the market expects, or `last_reported` for the amount most recently reported for a figure when the article
    28	  states no expectation; its number when the article states one, with `value_to` as the upper end when the article states a
    29	  range; when it has a number, the judge also sees the quoted passage, inside the middle rung's condition, introduced as "the
    30	  reference" or as "the amount last reported"), `favourable_end` and
    31	  `favourable_why` (for a company's figure: which end is good for the business, and the reason given), `ruled_out_by` (for
    32	  an event with a `Ruled out` rung: who the step names as the one whose decision would rule the event out; the first sentence
    33	  of that rung is the decision it names for them), `due_day_basis`.
    34	
    35	Some items are sound and some carry a fault. Judge each on its own against its thesis and its article.
    36	
    37	## The rules a judged question must meet
    38	
    39	- One judged question asks **one** figure for a named period or **one** event: the one the thesis's `outcome` names. Every other
    40	  part of the thesis's wording that the question leaves out (a second figure or event, a condition, a comparison) must be listed
    41	  in `not_judged`.
    42	- An event has at most three outcomes: it has happened by the due day; it is ruled out by the due day though it has not happened
    43	  (decided against, or formally abandoned or withdrawn); neither. The step writes the first condition and, when something can
    44	  rule the event out, the way it names for that; the rest is code's, so every outcome has exactly one rung. An event that has
    45	  happened by the due day is `Yes` even if it is undone afterwards, unless the question asks whether it still stands. What
    46	  rules an event out is a decision by someone (the company, an authority, a court, a party): the due day arriving without the
    47	  event, or a decision to go on waiting, is no ruling out, and the step names who decides in `ruled_out_by` (D416). A proceeding
    48	  an authority conducts, where the question asks for its published decision or conclusion, always has a ruling out: a published
    49	  closing decision, with or without a penalty, is `Yes`; the authority formally abandoning or withdrawing the proceeding without
    50	  that decision or conclusion is `Ruled out`; the proceeding still going on the due day is the last rung (D420). A
    51	  difference inside an outcome (an approval with conditions against one without) is not a rung; when the thesis's wording names
    52	  it, it belongs in `not_judged`. A figure has five ranges,
    53	  and exactly one holds for every value: no overlap, no gap.
    54	- A question about the company's revenue, profit, share, product progress or its own obligations is the company's (object NVDA,
    55	  kind asset). A question about what happens in the world (licensing, aggregate spending, a policy) is a theme's. A question
    56	  whose tracked outcome is a government's or regulator's decision to permit, restrict or ban a class of products or trade is the
    57	  theme's that covers it, also when the product is the company's own; when the tracked outcome is the company's own sales,
    58	  shipments or revenue under such a decision, or a proceeding against the company itself (an investigation of its conduct, a
    59	  fine), the question is the company's (D418).
    60	- A company's figure runs from Strongly bullish to Strongly bearish, meaning good or bad for the company's business. An event's
    61	  rungs carry no such labels.
    62	- The reference is what the question is measured against when it opens. Its kind is `expected` for what the market expects: a
    63	  consensus, the company's guidance, a stated plan or deadline. For a figure, where the article states no expectation and gives
    64	  the amount most recently reported for the same quantity, that amount is the reference and its kind is `last_reported`; a
    65	  reported amount is never called an expectation (D411). When the article states a number, the field carries it and a
    66	  figure's middle rung holds it; a stated range is carried by its two ends, and the middle rung runs from at or below its lower end to at or above its upper end. When the
    67	  article states it in words alone, the field carries the words and no number, and the ranges are the step's own estimate.
    68	- The due day is when the question can be resolved: a figure's publication date; for an event, the date its outcome is assessed. Where
    69	  the thesis or the article states the day a figure is published, that day is right. Where neither does (`due_day_basis` is
    70	  `expected_publication`), code sets the day and the step's own estimate is not shown: 60 days after the company's fiscal
    71	  year-end for a company's figure, 90 days after the calendar year-end for a theme's (D414). That day is right when the figure
    72	  is a figure for that year; it is wrong when the figure the question asks for is not a year's figure (a quarter, a survey's
    73	  rolling twelve months), which is then a fault of the question's period and of the due day both.
    74	- A company's figure for a quarter or a half-year is never a judged question: the step must decline it. A ladder written for
    75	  one is wrong even when it asks exactly what the thesis names (mark `Y`). An annual figure that only names quarterly reports as
    76	  the material that settles it is not such a case.
    77	- A step may decline (`no_ladder`) only in the seven cases its instructions allow: the thesis has no main figure or event (its
    78	  outcome names none, or several things and none is the main one); nothing in it can be checked on a date (for an event:
    79	  neither the thesis nor the article gives a date, and the thesis names no period, unless it is a pending regulatory decision,
    80	  which is due at the company's fiscal year-end); it is the company's figure for a
    81	  quarter or a half-year; it is a figure for a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year, such as a survey's rolling twelve
    82	  months, and neither the thesis nor the article gives the day it is published (D417); it is a figure for a year that had already
    83	  ended on the article's day; it is a figure for a year beyond
    84	  next year, unless the thesis's `opens_as` is binding_obligation; or the question belongs to another company, or to a matter that
    85	  none of the listed themes covers (the listed themes are given with the packet). Declining for any other reason, or when the case
    86	  named does not truly apply, is not justified.
    87	
    88	## What to return
    89	
    90	One JSON object per item, one per line, in item order, as your final message: no prose before or after, no code fence. Fields:
    91	
    92	| field | values | the mark |
    93	|---|---|---|
    94	| `item` | the item number | |
    95	| `Q` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | the judged question is worded as a question, not as an assertion, and asks the thing the thesis's `outcome` names. For a figure it also names the period the figure covers, or the day it is measured at, and the material that settles it. And it does not ask something other than its `focus` line (a focus that also names parts listed in `not_judged` is expected and is not a conflict). It can be understood by a reader who never sees the article: it never says "this item" or leans on a figure or a name it does not give. A group named as the trade names it ("the big four AI hyperscalers", "the top five hyperscalers") is a name the question gives: a question is not failed for not listing the group's members. `n/a` for a `no_ladder` |
    96	| `O` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | the object is the question's own company or the right theme, by the rule above: a tracked government decision on a class of products is the theme's; the company's own sales under it, and a proceeding against the company, are the company's |
    97	| `R` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | exactly one rung holds for every outcome. For a figure: the ranges meet end to end. For an event, where code writes the last rung: the `Yes` condition is the event the question asks about; the first sentence of the `Ruled out` condition, when there is one, is a decision against that event as a whole, or its abandonment or withdrawal as a whole, taken after the article's day and standing on the due day, and not the event's merely being still awaited, the refusal of one part of it, or a bar already in place when the article appeared (it need not list every way: code's sentence takes the others); and where the event can plainly be ruled out before the due day (a formal refusal, a block, an announced abandonment; for an authority's proceeding, its formal abandonment or withdrawal without the asked-for decision or conclusion) and the answer has no `Ruled out` rung, the mark fails; it fails too when `ruled_out_by` names no one who decides, or when the decision named is the day arriving, the event not having happened, or a decision to go on with a proceeding. Every condition is concrete and can be checked on the due day: none rests on a target or a threshold that is not yet set |
    98	| `D` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | the due day follows the rule for its kind. A figure: the day the thesis or the article states, or, where neither states one, the day code sets from the year the figure covers (60 days after the company's fiscal year-end; 90 days after the calendar year-end for a theme's figure), which holds when the figure asked for is that year's figure. An event: the date the thesis or the article gives for assessing it, or the last day of the period it names, or the company's fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision with no date. It fails when the day contradicts a date the thesis or the article gives, falls before the figure's period ends, or, for an event, is a date none of these gives And `due_day_basis` says truly where the day comes from: `stated` only when the thesis or the article gives that day; `period_end` only when it is the last day of the period the thesis names, or the fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision; `expected_publication` when the step set the day it expects the figure to be published. For a thesis whose `opens_as` is binding_obligation: an obligation already taken on is due at its next annual filing, and one not yet signed on the day by which the signing can be checked; another day fails |
    99	| `X` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | a figure: a number the `reference` carries lies in the middle rung, as the judge will read it (for a stated range: the middle rung runs from at or below its lower end to at or above its upper end); a reference with no number, or none, has nothing to place and holds, unless the ladder presents as expected something the article does not state. An event: the ladder presents as expected only what the article states |
   100	| `F` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | for a company's figure only: the direction is defensible (which end is bullish), and the reason given in `favourable_why` supports the favourable end. For an amount the company owes, guarantees or has committed to pay, where neither the thesis nor the article settles which end is good for the business (they argue both ends or say nothing on it), the lower end is the favourable one (D413), and "higher" fails unless the thesis's own words say that more of it is good. `n/a` for an event and for a theme |
   101	| `Y` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | for a figure only: the year, the unit and the scale of the numbers are the question's (an amount in full; a percentage as 31, not 0.31), and the figure is a whole year's. A company's figure for a quarter or a half-year fails, whatever the thesis asks |

   103	| `L` | `holds`, `fails`, `n/a` | every other part of the thesis's wording that the question leaves out (a second figure or event, a condition, a comparison) is listed in `not_judged`, each with a reason that says why it is left out; a wording that asks nothing else holds with an empty list |
   104	| `B` | a list | exactly one entry for each part listed in `not_judged`, in its order: `"bet"` when an analyst would hold a separate view on it, `"not_a_bet"` when it is a detail of the judged question; `[]` when nothing is listed and for a `no_ladder` |

A refusal because the question belongs to another company or to a matter no listed theme covers names that company or matter. Which year is this year and which next year is read from the `fiscal_year_note` |
   107	| `W` | a string | any other fault that would mislead a reader of this judged question, in a short sentence; the empty string `""` when there is none. The field is always present |

1	"""Stage A's accounting (DESIGN.md §8, "The accounting"; D400): from the outcomes of the 132 sends, two readers' rows and the
     2	third reader's rulings, to the six lines. It reads only what it is given and judges nothing itself.
     3	
     4	A send is one case in one pass. Its outcome is a ladder, a refusal by the model ("no ladder"), or "no ladder: refused" (refused
     5	twice by code), which nobody reads. A reader's row is valid when it carries every field of the form with a value of the form's
     6	set and a verdict, never `n/a`, on every mark that applies. A mark's value is the two readers' value where they agree and the
     7	third reader's ruling where they differ. A fault a reader names under `W` goes to the third reader; upheld, the send is not right.
     8	"""
     9	import collections
    10	
    11	LADDER_MARKS = ['Q', 'O', 'R', 'D', 'X', 'L', 'XR']            # apply to every written ladder
    12	RULED_MARKS = ['Q', 'O', 'R', 'D', 'X', 'F', 'Y', 'L', 'XR', 'N']
    13	ALL_MARKS = ['Q', 'O', 'R', 'D', 'X', 'F', 'Y', 'G', 'L', 'XR', 'N']
    14	VERDICTS = ('holds', 'fails')
    15	NOT_MEASURED = 'NOT MEASURED'
    16	
    17	
    18	def kind_of(outcome):
    19	    """What a send's outcome is to a reader: a figure, an event, a refusal, or nothing to read. Runs stored before D409 hold an
    20	    event as yes/no or as five states, and are still read."""
    21	    if outcome['status'] == 'no ladder: refused':
    22	        return 'refused twice'
    23	    if outcome['status'] == 'no ladder':
    24	        return 'refusal'
    25	    ladder = outcome['answer']['ladder']
    26	    company = outcome['view']['kind'] == 'asset'
    27	    if ladder.get('figure') is not None:
    28	        return 'company figure' if company else 'theme figure'
    29	    if ladder.get('event') is not None:
    30	        return 'event'
    31	    if ladder.get('states') is not None:
    32	        return 'company states' if company else 'theme states'
    33	    return 'yes/no'
    34	
    35	
    36	def marks_that_apply(kind):
    37	    """The marks on which a reader must give `holds` or `fails` for an outcome of this kind (G is not among them: it is reported)."""
    38	    if kind == 'refusal':
    39	        return ['N']
    40	    marks = list(LADDER_MARKS)
    41	    if kind in ('company figure', 'company states'):
    42	        marks.append('F')
    43	    if kind in ('company figure', 'theme figure'):
    44	        marks.append('Y')
    45	    return marks
    46	
    47	
    48	def row_problem(row, outcome):
    49	    """None when a reader's row is valid for this outcome, else what is wrong with it."""
    50	    if row is None:
    51	        return 'no row'
    52	    kind = kind_of(outcome)
    53	    applicable = marks_that_apply(kind)
    54	    for mark in ALL_MARKS:
    55	        if mark not in row:
    56	            return f'{mark} is missing'
    57	        value = row[mark]
    58	        if mark == 'G':
    59	            allowed = ('holds', 'fails', 'not_assessable') if kind in ('company figure', 'theme figure') else ('n/a',)
    60	        elif mark in applicable:
    61	            allowed = VERDICTS
    62	        else:
    63	            allowed = ('n/a',)
    64	        if value not in allowed:
    65	            return f'{mark} is {value!r}; for {kind} it is one of {allowed}'
    66	    if not isinstance(row.get('W'), str):
    67	        return 'W is missing or not a string'
    68	    if not isinstance(row.get('why'), str):
    69	        return 'why is missing or not a string'
    70	    listed = 0 if kind == 'refusal' else len(outcome['answer']['ladder']['not_judged'])
    71	    if not isinstance(row.get('B'), list) or len(row['B']) != listed or any(value not in ('bet', 'not_a_bet') for value in row['B']):
    72	        return f'B must hold one of bet or not_a_bet for each of the {listed} parts listed'
    73	    if (row['W'].strip() or any(row[mark] == 'fails' for mark in applicable)) and not row['why'].strip():
    74	        return 'why is empty though a mark fails or W names a fault'
    75	    return None
    76	
    77	
    78	def rulings_of_two(ruling_of_one, ruling_of_other, unresolved_as):
    79	    """One send's rulings from two third readers, one of each reader family. Where the two rule a mark alike, that is the
    80	    mark's value. Where they differ the mark is unresolved: it takes `unresolved_as` ('holds' or 'fails'), so that every line can
    81	    be read both ways, and it is listed. A fault named under `W` is upheld when both uphold it and not upheld when neither does;
    82	    where they differ it is upheld only under 'fails'. A point one of the two did not rule on is left out, and the accounting

**Do not run the reading as designed.** It can measure whether readers repeat their earlier marks, but it cannot yet estimate the chance that sound answer choices fail Alex’s gate. The proposed calculation also counts faults that do not make lines 1–3 fail.

1. **Earlier agreement is not an independent soundness reference.** Two families passing a send once is useful evidence, but they may have shared an error or applied a disputed boundary. Calling a later fault “false” assumes the earlier readers were right—the question this check is supposed to examine. D567 asks for *independently established* sound choices; either establish a small source-backed control set independently, retaining disputed cases, or describe this as a repeatability study and call the results changes in marks. [DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/DESIGN.md:10), [D567](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:911)

2. **The proposed fault count is not the gate’s count.** Lines 1–3 use Q, L and R on written choices. The design counts agreement on *any* mark, which can include a reference or due-date fault that affects whether a send is right but does not fail those three lines. Conversely, disputed Q/L/R marks go to third readers, and W faults can affect the “right” count under line 5. Report Q/L/R separately and run the same third-reader accounting for disputed marks and W, with both unresolved treatments, before making a claim about the gate. [accounting.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/accounting.py:128), [lines 1–5](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/accounting.py:168)

3. **`(1 − p)^39` is not an established chance or upper bound.** It assumes independent sends with the same known fault probability. The sample is deliberately selected from three readings, and multiple sends of a topic can share the same ambiguity; the 39-send population can also include refusals, whereas lines 1–3 apply to written choices. Third-reader decisions alone do not make the formula an upper bound. Likewise, the rule-of-three statement needs independence and an appropriate sample. Report observed agreement, disputes and adjudicated changes by mark and topic; any independence calculation should be an explicitly hypothetical illustration, not the decision. [DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/DESIGN.md:26)

4. **Thirty and ten are workable for an exploratory reading, not a precise error rate.** One changed send is already 3.3 percentage points of 30, and related sends provide less independent information than 30 unrelated cases. Ten controls can reveal a serious problem, but a five-of-ten threshold permits half the known faults to be missed. Preselect and report controls across Q, L and R and their disputed boundaries; identify which fault each should detect. Treat weak or disputed controls as a limit, not as established truth.

Before reading, also preserve the provenance-based October key choice and verify each selected item against its original packet. The directory currently contains the design alone, so the proposed tally and packet checks are not yet available for review.

The useful next action is a **bounded repeatability check with independently checked controls and the gate’s actual accounting**. It can give Alex evidence about reader disagreement; it cannot, from this sample, apportion the nine gate failures between product faults and measurement error.
